neighbours.label: the start of an aside right after a year: 'open since 1996 – a nice long run', 'opened in 1932 – a remarkable feat', 'since 2004, a fact…'; a year followed by ', and …' or an aside after a non-date stays quiet (the - pole takes 'over time and space'-type pairs)
fire: The bakery has been in the family since 1961 – a proud record for a small town.
The tunnel was finished in 1988 – a huge achievement for its engineers.
He has coached the side since 2009, a spell that brought three titles.
The magazine has appeared every month since 1975 – an impressive run by any measure.
The dam was completed in 1936 – a triumph of planning during hard times.
They have been married since 1994, a fact that still surprises their friends.
The festival has been held here since 2001 – a tradition the village loves.
The record has stood since 1968 – a remarkably long time in athletics.
quiet: The bakery has been in the family for ages – a proud record for a small town.
The tunnel was finished on schedule – a huge achievement for its engineers.
He has coached the side with patience, a style that brought three titles.
The magazine has appeared every month without fail – an impressive run by any measure.
The dam was completed in 1936, and the valley behind it slowly filled.
They have been married since 1994 and still live in the same flat.
The festival has been held here every summer – a tradition the village loves.
The record has stood unbroken – a remarkably long spell in athletics.

notes: Card: no single token; peaks on ' a', ',', '.', ' is', ' of' just after a date or duration ('since 1996 – a', 'last December,', 'in 1806, that is'). Probes: 'since 1996 – a' 0.71, 'since 2004, a fact' 0.44, 'in 1932 – a remarkable' 0.44, 'last December,' 0.44; 'in 1945, and' 0.03, 'on Tuesday, a little' 0.06, 'on Main Street – a' 0.01, 'last March, nobody' 0.01.
